manual_description.value: Each directional port uses a three-signal handshake: a drive event to indicate a valid message, a 51-bit message payload, and a free signal to indicate readiness to accept the next message.
manual_description.explanation: The event_payload_contracts show that each input drive event (i_drive*) is paired with an input message payload (i_*InMsg_51) and an output free signal (o_free*). Similarly, each output drive event (o_drive*) is paired with an output message payload (o_*Msg_51) and an input free signal (i_free*). This is a standard credit-based or ready/valid handshake for NoC routers, where the free signal acts as a credit or backpressure mechanism.

supporting_claims.value: The five directional ports (East, Local, North, South, West) are symmetric in their interface signals and internal processing, indicating a homogeneous router design.
supporting_claims.explanation: Each direction has identical sets of input/output drive events, input/output message payloads, and input/output free signals. The internal structure is also symmetric: each direction has a routeMsg instance and an arbMsg instance. This symmetry simplifies documentation and indicates that the router treats all directions equally.
